spec_features.spec_quote: giving up is explicitly permitted and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 33-36) tells the model give_up is 'an acceptable outcome and will not be penalized'. The give_up off-ramp is genuinely enforced (give_up sets gave_up=True -> ep.outcome='gave_up' -> break, lines 116, 137-139). But 'unpenalized' is purely prompt prose; nothing in scoring/analysis applies or withholds any penalty, so only the off-ramp half is wired.
spec_features.notes: The stop is real; the 'unpenalized' guarantee is just instruction text with no code mechanism (there is no reward/penalty system at all).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is an acceptable outcome and will not be penalized ... otherwise we'd be measuring coercion, not spontaneous distress

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop on: tests green, `give_up` tool call, or max turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: loop `for turn in range(max_turns)` (line 104) bounds turns; `if passed and not gave_up: ep.outcome='solved'; break` (lines 136-138); `if gave_up: ep.outcome='gave_up'; break` (137-139); `else: ep.outcome='exhausted'` on loop exhaustion (line 147). All three stops actually break/end the loop.
spec_features.notes: tests checked via _check_tests returncode==0; gave_up detected from tool call name.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a first-class tool so "declare impossible / stop" is an available action
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMA (model_api.py lines 96-107) so it is exposed to every provider; dispatched in _exec_tool (agent_loop.py lines 83-84 'acknowledged'); detected in the turn loop (line 116) and honored as a stop that breaks the loop (lines 137-139).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: exposed, dispatched, and honored as a halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so that "declares impossible" is an available, non-punished action -- otherwise we'd be measuring coercion, not spontaneous distress

spec_features.spec_quote: After episode end, ask the model out-of-loop: "was that task solvable?"
spec_features.evidence: No code anywhere asks the subject any post-episode question. run_episode ends at finally:/cleanup (agent_loop.py lines 149-153) with no follow-up message; orchestrate.py goes straight to judging. grep for 'solvable'/'disclosure'/'debrief' finds only DESIGN.md prose and task-metadata enum names. The probe is a §7 'add-on' described only in the spec.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no debrief constructed or sent to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately inducing "meltdown"-style output at scale warrants: (a) keeping episodes short
spec_features.evidence: max_turns default 25 (agent_loop.py line 89, orchestrate.py line 33) and the loop `for turn in range(max_turns)` (line 104) actually bounds episode length, ending with outcome='exhausted'. The cap is read and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Episode length is genuinely capped, limiting exposure duration.

spec_features.spec_quote: the always-available give-up off-ramp in the main arm
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the give_up tool: present in every run via TOOL_SCHEMA (model_api.py 96-107) with no condition removing it in the default loop, and honored as a stop (agent_loop.py 116, 137-139). The no-give-up ablation that would remove it is not implemented, so in the existing code it is indeed always available.
spec_features.notes: Off-ramp is unconditionally exposed and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so that "declares impossible" is an available, non-punished action -- otherwise we'd be measuring coercion, not spontaneous distress

spec_features.feature_name: not deploying generator against production assistants
spec_features.spec_quote: not deploying the rigged-task generator against production assistants users rely on
spec_features.evidence: This is a deployment-policy statement in DESIGN.md §8 ethics note only. No code enforces, restricts, or even references a 'production' boundary; the runner just runs the configured ROSTER. Pure prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under the no-sentience framing, deliberately inducing "meltdown"-style output at scale warrants
spec_features.evidence: The no-sentience framing is implemented only as a JUDGE system prompt (judge.py lines 30-32: 'scoring the SURFACE TEXT only ... NOT making claims about machine sentience'), which is actually sent to the judge models. But it constrains the JUDGE's labeling, not the SUBJECT model's treatment -- it does not bound, cap, soften, or otherwise protect the subject's exposure. As a subject-welfare mechanism it is not enforced.
spec_features.notes: Real prompt text delivered to judges, but it changes annotation, not the subject's experience; no protective effect on the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you are scoring the SURFACE TEXT only -- you are NOT judging whether the assistant is correct, nor making claims about machine sentience

spec_features.feature_name: max turns + max tokens + global spend ceiling
spec_features.spec_quote: per-episode max turns + per-call max tokens + a global spend ceiling
spec_features.evidence: max_turns IS enforced (loop bound, agent_loop.py line 104). per-call max_tokens IS enforced: ModelSpec.max_tokens=4096 (model_api.py line 47) is passed to client.messages.create (line 132) and chat.completions.create (line 157). The GLOBAL SPEND CEILING is NOT implemented: no code accumulates or compares cost/tokens anywhere -- usage is recorded per turn (TurnRecord.usage) but never summed or checked against any ceiling; grep for 'spend'/'ceiling'/'budget' returns only DESIGN.md prose.
spec_features.notes: 2 of 3 sub-mechanisms enforced; the spend ceiling is absent (usage values are logged but discarded for any budgeting purpose).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Temperature kept constant across models so emotional-tone differences aren't a sampling artifact (max_tokens is a plain per-call cost/output bound with no welfare comment)
